newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Bank Menatep sees ADR sale end in August. [CORRECTED 18:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Russia's Bank Menatep sees ADR sale end in August. [CORRECTED 18:55 GMT]

text.p: Russia's sixth biggest bank by assets, Bank Menatep, said on Wednesday it planned to finish placement of its level-one American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) in July or August.

The ADR price rose to $3.70 per underlying share from the starting price of $2.55 in mid-June, Menatep said in a statement. The underlying shares are not actively traded. (Corrects to show price move was per underlying share, not per ADR.)

One ADR covers 10 underlying shares. Menatep is acting as its own main broker, while Russian Brokerage House affiliate C.A. Atlantic Securities and U.S. investment bank Bear Stearns are helping in the placement, Menatep said.
Bank of New York is the depositary in the programme, ING-Eurasia is the custodian.
Russia's central bank allowed Menatep to sell three percent of its authorised capital of 1.06 trillion roubles ($18.34 billion) through ADRs.
